decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to the lone left tube, raising and pitching the left wrist; right arm remains parked.
Continue a smooth elbow-up reach toward the left tube, progressively pitching down while moving forward; recheck before grasp descent.
Align the left gripper with the tube axis and lower to the grasp height, keeping it open until the wrist view confirms centering.
Refine wrist pitch and lateral alignment before closing; tube is not yet centered in the wrist view.
Use small wrist-view corrections to center the tube between the open jaws and reduce its image tilt.
Finish fine centering and close the left gripper on the tube body; retention will be checked during lift.
Lift the closed left gripper up and back to clear the table, checking that the tube remains between the jaws.
Tube appears retained. Carry it inward while gradually rotating upright, preserving the elbow-up branch and table clearance.
Continue rotating the held tube toward vertical above the rack's left side; keep the right arm still.
Finish bringing the retained tube upright above a left-side rack slot, then check alignment before descending.
Lower the upright tube toward the left rack opening, pausing above full insertion depth for visual alignment.
Continue a slow vertical insertion approach with the tube retained; inspect the rack opening as it enters view.
The tube shifted upward in the jaws during descent, suggesting rim contact. Lift clear and shift slightly right and forward toward the large opening.
Test the corrected alignment with a controlled vertical descent, keeping the tube closed in the gripper.
Lower the final small distance, then open to let the upright tube settle into the opening; verify seating visually before withdrawal.
Withdraw the open left gripper upward and back without touching the tube, to inspect whether it settles upright in the rack.
The released tube is leaning rather than fully seated. Approach its upper body with open jaws to regrasp and straighten it.
Advance the open jaws around the leaning tube's body and close gently in position control to recover it.
Close fully, lift the tube slightly free of the rim, and rotate the wrist back upright before reinsertion.
The tube is retained and straighter. Lower vertically toward the same large slot, watching for renewed rim contact.
Continue the slow vertical insertion with the straighter grasp, stopping for another view before release.
The tube slipped sideways onto the rack. Open and lift away to inspect its resting orientation before attempting recovery.
Clear the left arm from the rack and begin an elbow-up approach to the inner right tube. The displaced left tube will need recovery later.
Advance and pitch the right wrist toward the inner tube, while returning the empty left arm toward its home side.
Lower the right gripper toward the inner tube with small pitch and centering corrections; keep the jaws open for the final visual check.
Fine-center the inner right tube using wrist feedback and bring the left arm close to its starting pose.
The right tube is centered between the jaws. Make a small along-axis correction and close before lifting.
Lift the closed right gripper away from the tabletop and verify tube retention before rotating toward the rack.
Tube is retained. Begin carrying it inward and rotating upright with a continuous elbow-up trajectory.
Continue the retained tube's smooth inward transfer and upright rotation, with clearance above the rack.
Finish rotating the right-held tube upright above the rack's right side; recheck the slot alignment before lowering.
Align slightly inward with the rightmost large slot and lower the upright tube to just above seating height.
Lower straight into the right-side opening while retaining the tube, checking for any slip or rim contact.
Rim contact is visible from tube motion relative to the jaws. Lift clear, then shift forward toward the large right-front hole before another descent.
Lower to the corrected opening and release without further pushing, allowing the tube to settle; inspect its depth and uprightness next.
Keep the jaws fully open while the tube settles, then withdraw a short distance to inspect seating without pushing it.
The released right tube toppled. Clear the right arm for an unobstructed rack view while beginning an elbow-up recovery approach to the displaced left tube.
Approach the displaced left tube from above while returning the empty right arm toward its own home workspace.
Bring the left wrist down over the displaced tube for visual centering; complete the right arm's retreat without crossing workspaces.
Replan from the interrupted pose with much smaller forward increments, lowering first to preserve elbow-up continuity and reach margin.
Use small forward and lateral corrections to bring the displaced left tube into the open jaws, monitoring reach and rack clearance.
Forward reach hit a continuity limit. Retract slightly and use a shallower wrist angle to reach the tube body without extending the arm further.
Center over the near body of the displaced tube with a shallow approach and close, avoiding further forward pushing.
The jaws are at the tapered end rather than the body. Reopen and use a shallower approach to reach farther along the tube while reducing arm extension.
Try retaining the near end and draw it back into easier reach, with a small lift to avoid dragging across the rack.
Reopen after the missed pinch and correct the lateral offset toward the tube body, using small motions from the observed pose.
Recenter the tube from the current wrist image and align the open jaws with its axis using small lateral and yaw corrections.
Hold wrist orientation fixed and correct the remaining lateral offset with open jaws; monitor the tube rather than closing on its tip.
The tube seems to move with an open finger rather than recenter. Lift and back away to disengage contact before another grasp approach.
With the fingers clear, make a fixed-orientation lateral correction toward the tube and verify the wrist-image response.
The clear-view lateral test showed the required direction. Shift left above the tube while keeping the open fingers clear of contact.
